title: Seeing Like an Agent — Anthropic Tool Design Philosophy (First-Party)
description: Official Anthropic engineering post by Thariq Shihipar (published April 10, 2026) documenting the internal methodology for designing AI agent tools. Key principles: (1) 'progressive disclosure' — tools should surface just enough information for the agent to act without flooding context; (2) 'seeing like an agent' — design tools by reasoning through the agent's perceptual model, not a human's; (3) even well-designed tools fail if Claude can't discover or invoke them correctly. Concrete case studies: AskUserQuestion (blocking modal that prevents conversation-buried clarifications), Task tool (context-isolated delegation). Primary source, not a third-party summary. High integration value: the progressive disclosure principle directly applies to agent/skill SKILL.md design, MCP tool description authoring, and the 2KB cap strategy.
